newsitem.title: UK: London precious metals markets await option expiry.
newsitem.headline: London precious metals markets await option expiry.

text.p: Attention focused on the over the counter (OTC) options expiry due later on Thursday, putting precious metals markets on hold ahead of the event.
Dealers said the big strike price for gold was the $340.00 per ounce call, which was well out of the money on Thursday morning when gold fixed at $337.90 compared with $338.45 previously.
"The $340 is the main strike price people are talking about, but if $337.25 or under is probed then we could see pressure on the $335.00 strike," one dealer said.
That could bring out option related selling as option players tried to make the best of their positions, he said.
There was little overnight news to stimulate the markets and the foreign exchanges were steady during early Europe.
Light fund selling late on New York's Comex took the gold futures price off its early high and the Far East markets did little more than hold levels in routine business, dealers said.
The very bearish sentiment of the past few weeks remained but some dealers were beginning to see a chink of light, albeit through a prism rather than directly.
"Gold is showing all the signs that we are at the lows -- it is unfashionable, nobody wants it, and technically it isn't too clever either," a dealer said.
Another of the same mind added, "It's not going to go up in a straight line but every four to six weeks there will be a short covering rally."
He added that nobody wanted to be long just now, so a sharp jump on any change was quite likely.
"Gold needs to consolidate in the low $340s," he added.
However, some dealers said they were looking for an increase in producer selling as some miners stepped in to fulfil first half quotas before the end of June.
Silver was within a cent of unchanged all morning at $4.77/$4.79, having failed to break $4.80 earlier in the week.
"When it moves, its moves are exaggerated because people are in the wrong position," a dealer said.
The platinum group metals (PGMs) were also close to unchanged with platinum at $418.00/$422.00, down $0.50, and palladium at $193.00/$197.00, down $3.50.
"This is the level platinum reached on the way up before it went flying. Now that its back down you would expect it to steady around here," a dealer said.
There was still no sign of Russia's delayed 1997 PGM exports, due to begin within days, actually starting, dealers said
